title: Duchenne and Becker muscular dystrophy
everyday_terms: big calf muscles and weak legs
summary: Duchenne and Becker muscular dystrophy cause muscles to weaken over time, because the body cannot make enough of a protein called dystrophin. Duchenne usually starts in early childhood; Becker is milder and starts later.
inheritance_plain: It is X-linked: the DMD gene is on the X chromosome. Boys have one X, so one changed copy affects them. Girls have two X chromosomes and are usually carriers, though some have signs too. X-linked chances depend on which parent has the change, so a genetic counsellor talks them through with you.
carrier_meaning: A woman with one changed copy is called a carrier. Many carriers have no symptoms, but some have muscle weakness or heart changes, so heart checks are often offered.
disease_meaning: These conditions mostly affect boys. Care from specialist neuromuscular teams, including heart and breathing checks, physiotherapy and newer treatments, helps people stay active and well for longer.
screening: A genetic test can look for a change in the DMD gene. A genetic counsellor can explain who in a family might choose to be tested.
suggested_questions: Why is Duchenne muscular dystrophy more common in boys?
